title: Q-WORK-RESUME-1: a work record in state resume has an owner (server-lane) and no loop that works it
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** failure-audit and the daily fleet pass; any work record in state `resume` older than its priority's SLA
**Done check:** cmd:git grep -q worklog -- foundation/executor.py
**Status:** open

Audit 2026-11-28 (ultrastable/ultrastable, 51 open issues, oldest from 2026-11-25): ten work records (#2467 to #2475 and #2495) have sat in state `resume`, owner `server-lane`, since 2026-11-26 14:39 with their done check unmet (#2467: https://ultrastable.github.io/base-rates/ and /open-questions/ still answer 404). `foundation/worklog.py` `reap` hands a silent record to `server-lane` once and posts "re-dispatched to the server lane to resume", but no executor, lane or handoff loop reads work records: only worklog.py, its workflow and its tests name them. `stale()` also skips records already in `resume`, so nothing re-dispatches them. A record in `resume` therefore has an owner in name and no loop that works it, which is the loose end WORK-RECORD-1 says it removes.

Fixed with this item (pull request that files it): `worklog reap` adds `queue`, and scripts/sla.sh plus foundation/issueloop.py exempted every `queue` issue as mirror-owned, so a record was neither probed nor aged; `Done when: GET <url> answer 200` was also not read as a probe. Both loops now treat a work record like any other issue.

Remaining: a consumer. A record in state `resume` becomes an executor task in driver order: the executor reads the record (goal, done check, next step, PRs), works it on a branch, and the record is finished by its own done check, or, past `stale_hours` times the SLA with the check still failing, gets one disposition comment naming the evidence and the closing probe (never silently dropped, never closed unmet).

**Closing probe:** cmd:git grep -q worklog -- foundation/executor.py

**Prediction:** spec_quality >= 0.7 within 336 h (read by `python3 -m foundation specgate --report`; this item closing by its done check keeps the share of well-specified open items at or above today's reading)

**Out of scope:** closing a record whose done check fails, raising `stale_hours` or the SLA to hide the age, or a second store for work records.
